sum: A six-day loop from Sundarijal along a forested ridge to Tharepati at 3,690 m, then down through the Hyolmo villages of Melamchi Gaun, Tarkeghyang and Sermathang.

guide.note: The Nepal Tourism Board has required foreign trekkers to hire a licensed guide since April 2023, though checks on the trail are inconsistent. On this route a guide is most useful for finding the footpath where new jeep tracks have cut the old trail, and for arranging transport out from Sermathang or Melamchi.

access: The walking starts inside the Kathmandu Valley. Sundarijal is about 15 km from Thamel, under an hour by taxi or a little longer by local bus. At the far end, buses return from Melamchi Pul Bazaar in three to four hours, and jeeps can be arranged from Sermathang or Tarkeghyang when the dirt roads are dry.

photo.a: The scattered houses of Melamchi Gaun sit on a sunny shelf of terraced fields below a wall of forested mountains.
photo.c: Melamchi Gaun, a Hyolmo village in Helambu

includes: porter in most packages (the cheapest tiers leave one out)
Langtang and Shivapuri park permits and TIMS card
lodge beds and three meals a day on the trek

permits.name: Shivapuri Nagarjun National Park entry ticket
permits.fee: NPR 1,000 per person, per day and entry
permits.where: At the park gate, for example at Sundarijal.

permits.name: Langtang National Park entry permit
permits.where: At the park checkpoint in Dhunche on the drive to Syabrubesi, or in advance at the Tourist Service Centre in Bhrikutimandap, Kathmandu.

permits.name: Trekkers' Information Management System card
permits.where: Only through a registered trekking agency, which applies in the Nepal Tourism Board's online system with your route and your guide's details. Individual trekkers can no longer buy one over the counter.

transportText: A taxi shared by two from Kathmandu to Sundarijal
transportExtra: the bus back to Kathmandu from Melamchi Pul Bazaar
tips: Leave Kathmandu by 8 am on the first day. The climb to Chisapani is hotter and longer than it looks on the map.
Keep the Shivapuri ticket and the Langtang permit separate and to hand; they are checked by different posts, at Sundarijal and at Kutumsang.
Carry cash for the whole trek; do not count on an ATM anywhere on the route.
Trekking poles earn their place on days four and six, which are mostly steep descent.
Wear long socks and carry salt in the monsoon; the forest between Chisapani and Tharepati is thick with leeches.

days.t: Drive to Sundarijal, walk to Chisapani
days.note: Under an hour by road from Thamel, then stone steps beside the water pipeline, the Tamang village of Mulkharka and a long forest climb inside Shivapuri Nagarjun National Park to the Borlang Bhanjyang saddle. Chisapani is a short descent beyond it.

n: Hotel Trekkers paradise and Mountain View Restaurant

days.note: A day of ups and downs along the ridge: down 400 m to Pati Bhanjyang, up stone steps to Chipling, over a forested shoulder and down to Golphu Bhanjyang, then a last climb to Kutumsang, where permits are checked. You climb about 1,000 m in all to finish 300 m higher than you started.

A steady forest climb of about 1,200 m with no villages, only the lodges at Magin Goth after three hours or so. Rhododendron gives way to juniper and open pasture near the top. It is a big jump in sleeping height: if you are prone to headaches, stop at Magin Goth and finish in the morning.
why: Sleeping altitude rises 690 m, well over the 500 m guideline even with a rest night next to it.

days.note: Leave the Gosaikunda trail and drop more than 1,100 m through forest to Melamchi Gaun for lunch. Then descend again to the bridge over the Melamchi Khola at about 1,900 m and climb 700 m up the far side to Tarkeghyang. Sound knees matter more than lungs today.

The easiest day: a near-level contour through forest and past the small village of Gangyul, sharing parts of the way with a jeep track. You are in by lunch, with the afternoon free for Sermathang's monasteries and the view north to the Jugal peaks.

days.t: Sermathang to Melamchi Pul Bazaar, drive to Kathmandu
days.note: A descent of 1,700 m down the ridge through Kakani and Dubhachaur into rice terraces and real heat, much of it on or beside a jeep road. Buses then take three to four hours to Kathmandu. Many groups now skip the walk and ride down from Sermathang.
